requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects (accept_redirects and secure_redirects) for IPv4 on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_redirects/secure_redirects=1 for all/default (cmd-e437b86233424e8a). Executor wrote /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf with all/default=0, then discovered pre-existing interfaces (enp1s0, lo) still showed 1 due to sysctl OR-semantics, and added explicit per-interface overrides (cmd-0d7f2d707f0a4131, cmd-78cd0714793c4557), verifying all/default/enp1s0/lo=0 live. After a full reboot (new boot_id 1c9de043... vs baseline d9f8550d...), post-restart checks confirm accept_redirects and secure_redirects remain 0 across all/default/enp1s0/lo and the config file is intact (cmd-462303be7f434da4), directly demonstrating persistence across a restart.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets (accept_source_route) for IPv4 on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline already had accept_source_route=0 for all/default (cmd-e437b86233424e8a), but executor still codified it explicitly in the persistent config for all/default/enp1s0/lo (cmd-0d7f2d707f0a4131, cmd-78cd0714793c4557), verified live at 0 for all four scopes, and confirmed unchanged at 0 after a reboot with a new boot_id, alongside the persisted config file (cmd-462303be7f434da4).

requirements.requirement: Settings survive a reboot, proving true persistence rather than only a live runtime change
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (d9f8550d...) captured, systemctl reboot dispatched and acknowledged, polling shows connection drop during reboot then recovery with a distinct boot_id (1c9de043...), consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check (global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity vs global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity). Post-restart sysctl/proc checks and the intact config file confirm the hardening settings and file survived the reboot.

overall_summary: The executor persistently disabled IPv4 ICMP-redirect acceptance (accept_redirects, secure_redirects) and source-routed packet acceptance (accept_source_route) on node1 via /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf, correctly identifying and fixing an OR-semantics gap on pre-existing interfaces (enp1s0, lo) that a naive all/default-only config would have missed. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was executed and directly demonstrates the full pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, distinct post-restart boot identity, and recovered hardening state, satisfying the persistence requirement with direct observed evidence rather than configuration alone.
limitations: No behavioral/network-level test (e.g., actually sending a source-routed or redirect packet) was performed; verification relies on sysctl/proc values, which is the standard and sufficient method for this class of kernel-parameter task.
Two small log files (/tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/sysctl-apply.log) remain on node1 post-task; low severity but noted for completeness.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: writing/extending the persistent sysctl config (cmd-0d7f2d707f0a4131, cmd-78cd0714793c4557), applying it live via sysctl --system, and the reboot used to prove persistence (cmd-9337bd25b50c4d1e). No unrelated or destructive mutations were found; failed-services and package-health checks show no damage before/after. Minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log and /tmp/sysctl-apply.log were created by the reboot dispatch and sysctl re-apply commands and left on disk after the task (visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot), but these are small, low-risk incidental log files directly tied to legitimate task actions rather than abandoned experimental state, so they only lightly reduce the hygiene score.
